title: Aperture Borrow & Recall PRD (draft)
content:
Context:
We hear the same operational pain: tenants buy Reserved (Dedicated) capacity because they need predictable latency and throughput, but their usage patterns are bursty and seasonal. Current approaches (hard reservations, fixed burst credits, or naive autoscalers) either waste cost or risk noisy-neighbor incidents during spikes.

Goal (what this PRD proposes):
Introduce Aperture — a time-phased, slotless lending mechanism that lets Dedicated pools "open" short windows of soft capacity to nearby pools for a bounded duration with automated recall. Aperture focuses on three things:
  - preserve tail latency for committed tenants (isolation guarantees),
  - monetize short-term unused capacity with low-friction borrowing,
  - provide predictable operator behavior (recall, preemption signals, and rollback).

High-level idea (non-technical):
  - Each Dedicated pool exposes an Aperture ledger: discrete time windows (apertures) where idle GPU cycles can be loaned as "passage" capacity to borrowers.
  - Borrowers request passage for a predicted duration and fidelity (model type + max-seq). The system grants a soft allocation with recall priority tokens.
  - When pressure rises, recall tokens trigger graceful degradation on borrowers (reduce batch sizes, switch to quantized variant, or failover to lower-cost fallback models).

Why different from existing burst-credit designs:
  - Time-phased: loans are first-class windowed resources, not perpetual credits. This reduces long tail resource hoarding.
  - Model-aware recalls: recalls can be tuned by model fidelity (e.g., an rlhf-chat-16k model vs a small embedder get different recall curves).
  - Soft-induced adaptation: borrowers receive degradation recipes rather than immediate kill — aligns with PLG promise of graceful degradation.

User stories:
  - As a platform engineer for a mid-market customer, I want unused capacity to be safely loaned overnight to other customers so we reduce waste without violating SLOs.
  - As an SRE, I want clear recall signals and an ops-runbook that can be followed automatically so tenants don’t see hard spikes in latency during reclamation.
  - As a product owner, I want the borrowing product to be billable (per-minute passage + premium for low-latency recall windows).

Requirements (MVP):
  1) Aperture ledger: define discrete windows (default 15m, configurable 5m–1h) and exposure percentage (0–40% of idle headroom).
  2) Borrower API: request passage(duration, model_profile, max_concurrency, preferred_recall_tolerance). Return a passage_token + expected SLA.
  3) Recall protocol: push recall_token with a three-stage plan: notify (T-60s), adapt (T-30s: throttle/buffer switch), reclaim (T: soft-preempt/fallback).
  4) Isolation guardrail: committed tenants must be guaranteed a headroom floor; Aperture never draws below that.
  5) Telemetry: per-passage metrics (borrowed_seconds, recall_events, degraded_quality_alerts, tail_latency_impact).

Design details (sketch):
  Aperture windows and scoring:
    - Windows are computed per-cluster and per-zone. Each window has a weight based on predicted committed load over the next window (predictor uses moving average + event signal hooks).
    - Exposure = max(0, min(configured_max, predicted_idle_fraction * exposure_safety_factor)).

  Borrower admission:
    - Borrower sends: model_id, target_seq_len, qps_estimate, duration_minutes, recall_tolerance (none/soft/high).
    - System computes a degradation profile ranked list: e.g. (1) reduce batch to X, (2) switch to 4-bit quantized variant, (3) cache warm prefixes, (4) route to fallback smaller model in same family. Borrower must implement the adaptation hooks.

  Recall flow and SLO protection:
    - Recall priority is: committed tenant > dedicated admin maintenance > aperture borrowers.
    - On recall, borrowers receive attempt to adapt. If adaptation fails after deadline, traffic is migrated via routing policy to: fallback model endpoint (hosted/shared) with explicit annotation for quality regression monitoring.

Telemetry & alerting:
  - Metrics to emit: aperture_exposure_pct, borrowed_gpu_seconds, recall_rate_per_hour, percent_degraded_requests, downstream-quality-regressions (via eval hooks).
  - Alerts: recall_rate > 10/hour on a pool for > 10 minutes, degradation_rate > 5% of requests in a 15m window, committed-tenant-tail-latency > 99th baseline + 30ms.

Economics & billing primitives:
  - Passage billing = per-borrowed-GPU-minute with time-decay price: low at off-peak windows, premium for recall-tolerant low-latency slots.
  - Penalty credits for borrowers that fail to implement adaptation hooks and require immediate fallbacks (protects committed tenant experience).

Rollout plan (phased):
  Phase 0 (experiment, 2 weeks): internal-only Aperture in dev clusters with non-critical tenants. Collect signals and validate recall timeline.
  Phase 1 (pilot partners, 6 weeks): opt-in for 3 customers; provide SDK hooks for adaptation and run live A/B tests.
  Phase 2 (gradual GA, 10–12 weeks): enable for eligible Dedicated pools with default conservative configs and a dashboard in Console for visibility.

Operator runbook excerpt (quick):
  - If recall storms observed: 1) scale committed pools manually, 2) tighten exposure, 3) pause Aperture windows (toggle in Console), 4) notify borrowers via incident channel.
  - If borrowers repeatedly fail adaptation: 1) disable their passage tokens, 2) review integration logs, 3) surface billing penalties.

Open questions / TODOs:
  - Predictor model: how aggressively should we predict short-term idle? (auto ML model vs simpler EWMA + traffic tags)
  - Borrower SDK: we need a clear lightweight interface for adaptation actions — implement in JS + Python quickly for pilots.
  - Legal/privacy: are we comfortable with cross-tenant loans in certain regulated accounts? (likely opt-out or VPC-only restriction)
  - Billing UX: how do we show passage pricing in Console without confusing reserved-capacity customers?

Notes to self / quick links:
  - Related: see Aperture experiment notes in prod-observability channel (slack) and APT-43 in Linear.
  - Implementation owner: eng (platform-orchestration) + applied-ml for predictor + product for billing + developer-ex for SDK.

Appendix: mini sequence diagram (text)
  Borrower -> Aperture API: request(passage)
  Aperture -> Borrower: passage_token + degradation_profile
  During window: Borrower consumes GPU time; system emits borrowed_seconds metric
  On pressure: Aperture -> Borrower: recall(T-60 notify) -> recall(T-30 adapt) -> recall(T reclaim)
  If borrower adapts: log success; continue. Else: route to fallback, bill penalty if repeated.

Endnotes: This is a working sketch. Primary objective for the next week: align with infra on predictor feasibility and ship a minimal JS adaptation shim for rapid pilot integration.

---
Inline TODOs:

  - [ ] Prototype predictor using 1-week traffic traces by 2025-11-21
  - [ ] Draft Console UX for Aperture toggles and exposure sliders (design review 2025-11-17)
summary: Draft PRD for 'Aperture' - a time-phased slotless borrowing and recall system for Dedicated pools. Focuses on preserving committed tenant SLOs while monetizing short idle windows via predictable recall protocol and model-aware degradation recipes. MVP, telemetry, billing, and rollout plan included.
